ROOT CAUSE RESOLVED — PO triage 2026-07-29T08:48Z, occurrence #13 (sys-20260729T083834-4dd9, api-gateway:4000 A-12). This SPIKE's question is now ANSWERED from file evidence + router-measured raw state; no further isolation probing is needed before speccing the fix. VERDICT: neither branch of the original either/or. NOT a serving outage AND NOT a probe-side false positive. It is a deterministic BUDGET MISMATCH between two independently-authored 3000ms constants on a route that fans out to nine downstreams SEQUENTIALLY.

THE ARITHMETIC (all four cites captured this cycle):
(1) docs/agents/system-auditor/probe.sh:48 -- the A-12 probe is `curl ... --max-time 3 http://localhost:4000/health` and on any non-zero curl exit the `|| http_code="CURL_ERR"` fallback overwrites the real code. So CURL_ERR is emitted for a CLIENT-SIDE 3s timeout, indistinguishable in the output from a refused connection. NOTE: the tier-1 shell pre-gate scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:202 uses --max-time 6, but it probes ONLY ports 3000 (:479) and 3001 (:482) -- it never touches 4000, so its 6s budget is NOT the one that governs A-12. (2) apps/api-gateway/pkg/infrastructure/capability_prober.go:61-62 -- probeTTL = 60 * time.Second, probeTimeoutMs = 3000. The gateway's own PER-DOWNSTREAM probe budget is 3000ms, exactly equal to the auditor's WHOLE-REQUEST budget.

done_tasks.po_ruling_accept_new: PO RULING on the accept-new question. (1) REJECT `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` as the DURABLE answer — its stated justification is factually false. (2) KEEP it for now as a stopgap: reverting to `yes` today would simply re-break the tool, and nothing can be verified while the VPS is unreachable. done_tasks.evidence: git b741c5634 (merge of 1779c, 'QA APPROVED', 2026-04-30) — apps/mcp-server/Dockerfile contained BOTH `openssh-client` (line 23) and `ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]` (line 63). git 6165aa3b4 ('fix(docker): rebase Dockerfiles from Debian to Ubuntu to unblock builds') — BOTH GONE, with no mention in the commit message. apps/mcp-server/entrypoint.sh is still tracked and clean at HEAD but is COPY'd/referenced by NOTHING (`git log -S entrypoint.sh -- apps/mcp-server/Dockerfile` after the rebase = empty). So the premise 'this could never have succeeded since inception' is inverted: it was correctly configured at inception and was silently regressed by an unrelated Dockerfile rebase ~2.5 months ago.
done_tasks.why_accept_new_is_weaker_than_claimed: The sshExec.ts comment claims accept-new 'STILL rejects a CHANGED key on any later connection'. That protection is largely illusory HERE: docker-compose.yml mounts nothing at /root/.ssh, so known_hosts is ephemeral per-container. Every `docker compose up` starts with an EMPTY known_hosts, so it is trust-on-first-use on EVERY container recreate, not once — a MITM need only win the race after any restart, and restarts are routine (the container restarted twice today). TOFU-on-every-boot is materially weaker than the one-shot TOFU the comment describes.
done_tasks.also_rejects_the_other_objection: dev-mcp-server rejected build-time keyscan partly because it 'hardcodes the VPS IP'. The VPS IP is ALREADY hardcoded in docker-compose.yml in four places (VPS_HOST plus three proxy URLs), so this costs nothing new. Its second objection — that it couples the IMAGE BUILD to VPS reachability — is valid, and is exactly why the existing entrypoint.sh does the keyscan at CONTAINER START, not at build.
done_tasks.scope: (1) Restore `COPY apps/mcp-server/entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh` + `RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh` + `ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]` to apps/mcp-server/Dockerfile. (2) Revert sshExec.ts to StrictHostKeyChecking=yes ONCE seeding is live and proven. (3) Add a regression test asserting the Dockerfile still wires the entrypoint, so a future rebase cannot silently drop it again.
done_tasks.mandatory_change_do_not_restore_verbatim: entrypoint.sh as written is `set -e` + `exit 1` when ssh-keyscan yields nothing. Restoring it VERBATIM while the VPS is unreachable would make the mcp-server container FAIL TO BOOT — turning a VPS outage into a total outage of all 88 crons and the whole MCP tool surface. It MUST be changed to degrade non-fatally: log a loud WARN, leave known_hosts unseeded, let the server start, and let only the SSH-dependent tools fail loudly at call time. A VPS-reachability problem must never be able to prevent mcp-server startup.

done_tasks.title: 'Du bao AI & Ket qua' advertises a 66,7% hit-rate with no denominator and no exclusion reason — the figure is computed on 6 of 17 claims, all from Apr-May, frozen since 2026-06-21, and reads as live
done_tasks.root_cause: Live calibration block read from the served endpoint 2026-07-25T07:11:04Z: total=17, resolved=6, correct=4, wrong=2, pending=5, excluded=6, hitRate=0.6666666666666666, avgBrier=0.2135. The page renders 66,7% as the AI's accuracy. That number is 4/(4+2) over SIX claims — 35% of the population — while 6 are unscoreable and 5 unresolved. Worse than the small denominator: the six scored claims are ids 2,3,4,5,6,7, ALL created 2026-04-27 or 2026-05-03 and ALL resolved by 2026-06-21T16:35Z. Because every claim minted since 2026-06-14 has creation_price NULL, no new claim can ever enter the numerator or denominator — the badge is STRUCTURALLY FROZEN at 66,7% and has been for over a month, yet it carries no staleness marker and no denominator. A user reading the page cannot distinguish 'the AI is running at 66,7%' from 'the AI has not been scored in five weeks'. This is the passive-health-masks-dead-data pattern (feedback_passive_health_masks_dead_data.md): the green number is the reason nobody noticed the 6-week outage. PO POSITION: the user was right to distrust it. The badge as rendered overstates the track record, and the exclusion bucket that would have revealed the problem is a bare unexplained label.

(d) Show the full disposition breakdown (17 total = 4 dung + 2 sai + 5 dang cho + 6 loai tru) near the badge so the buckets always visibly sum to the total. (e) Vietnamese output must follow feedback_market_report_plain_vietnamese.md — plain language, decimal comma, no untranslated jargon.

MINTED 2026-07-25T16:31:11Z by po from 2x context_bloat_breach signals relayed by the coordinator (dev-team 16:07Z drain). RAW-verified at source before minting.

PREMISE CORRECTION FIRST — THE RELAYED DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG AND ACTING ON IT WOULD BUILD SOMETHING THAT ALREADY EXISTS. The relay states "the cap being denominated in the wrong unit regenerates them" and "the line cap is the enforced metric; bytes are what actually costs context". A BYTE CAP ALREADY EXISTS, IS CORRECT, AND IS FIRING — that is precisely what these two signals ARE (reason=byte-cap). scripts/agents-flow/context-bloat-backstop.sh:119-123 reads wc -c and compares against BYTE_CAP = MATCHED_CAP * 60 = 12000 (a 60 bytes/line budget), shipped as TE-T24; line 168 guarantees a size-justification header NEVER suppresses a byte-cap breach, specifically to close the mega-line evasion. Both units are measured. Do not re-derive a byte cap.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS AN ACTUATOR/DETECTOR ASYMMETRY — ONE CAP HAS AN ENFORCER, THE OTHER HAS ONLY AN ALARM.
  - LINE cap: detector PLUS an automatic actuator. scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh is a PostToolUse hook that drops the oldest "## " section in a loop until the file is back under cap. Its loop condition is line-only — early-exit at :135 `[ "$LINE_COUNT" -le 200 ] && exit 0`, loop-break at :174 `[ "$LINE_COUNT" -le 200 ] && break`. It never calls wc -c. Result: the line cap is self-healing and permanently satisfied.
  - BYTE cap: detector ONLY. The backstop hook emits a signal and stops. There is no actuator anywhere.
Agents therefore satisfy the enforced constraint by writing DENSER LINES, and nothing pushes back. alert-commander.md averages 632 bytes/line against a 60 bytes/line budget — 10.5x. The relay's instinct that "agents are complying with the cap and defeating its purpose" is exactly right; its explanation of why is not.

THE PRUNER IS NOT MERELY ABSENT ON THE BYTE AXIS — IT IS A CONTROL LOOP THAT STOPS AT THE WRONG SETPOINT. Dropping an oldest section reduces lines AND bytes together, so the existing actuator is perfectly capable of clearing a byte breach. It simply halts the instant lines <= 200, which on a dense file happens long before bytes <= 12000. The machinery is already built and already wired into the write path; only its stopping condition is on the wrong axis.

NON-CONVERGENCE, MEASURED — THIS IS WHY IT IS P1 DESPITE BEING SMALL. docs/signals/processed/ holds 87 context-bloat breach signals across 12 files: alert-commander 24, news-scout 12, system-auditor 10, architect 9, unified-agent 8, dev-mcp-server 8, agent-father 5, digest-predict 3, bctc-analyst 3, tran-ngoc-bau 2, decision-journal SKILL 2, qa 1. The 24 alert-commander fires span 2026-07-23T16:13Z to 2026-07-25T16:15Z — roughly every two hours for 48 hours — and the file is STILL 10x over and GREW 182->190 lines during the session that relayed this. Every one of those 87 signals was drained into processed/ and thereby marked handled while the measured condition was never touched. A detector whose output is filed rather than acted on is a detector that manufactures churn.

SCOPE IS 18 FILES, NOT THE 2 THAT SIGNALLED. po measured every notebook against the 12000-byte cap this tick. Over-cap, with bytes/line: alert-commander 120183B/190L/632, news-scout 62932B/198L/317, qa 55481B/187L/296, main 42582B/193L/220, digest-predict 39614B/148L/267, tran-ngoc-bau 38715B/188L/205, agent-father 29242B/326L/89, dev-team 23204B/85L/272, unified-agent 21153B/191L/110, architect 20169B/120L/168, pm 17670B/195L/90, dev-vps-crawls 15997B/168L/95, bctc-analyst 14162B/54L/262, dev-rag-service 13912B/185L/75, fixer 13690B/185L/74, dev-mainserver-crawls 13044B/144L/90, dev-mcp-server 12229B/49L/249, ba 12067B/51L/236. Note agent-father at 326L is ALSO over the line cap, so the line actuator is failing there for a separate reason worth one line in the fix's findings.

REMEDY — SMALL, DEFINITIF, AND IT SELF-HEALS THE BACKLOG. Change notebook-auto-prune.sh's early-exit (:135) and loop-break (:174) from a line-only condition to `lines > 200 OR bytes > 12000`, reading the byte cap with the same MATCHED_CAP * 60 derivation the backstop hook uses so the two stay in lockstep (do NOT hardcode 12000 twice — that is how the USD/VND three-SSOT defect happened). NO SEPARATE PRUNE TASK IS NEEDED for the sectioned notebooks: the corrected pruner fires on the next write to each file and rotates it back under both caps automatically, clearing ~16 of the 18 without human action. That is the whole point of fixing the actuator rather than the files.

THE ONE GENUINELY OPEN QUESTION, FOR THE IMPLEMENTER. The pruner has a safe-fail path (:179) for "only 1 section left and still over cap" that emits notebook_single_section_overage_breach and deliberately does NOT truncate. A byte setpoint makes that path newly reachable for files whose single current-cycle section alone busts 12000 bytes. Options: [a] keep the existing safe-fail behaviour, so the outcome is an honest signal rather than silent data loss — smallest change and consistent with the current contract; [b] additionally enforce the skill's ~60L-per-section rule on the byte axis. po did NOT choose. What is NOT acceptable is a pruner that truncates mid-section, which would destroy the current cycle's record.

SIBLING ROW — READ IT BEFORE STARTING. FIX-ALERT-COMMANDER-NOTEBOOK-SINGLE-BLOB-UNPRUNABLE covers alert-commander.md, which this fix CANNOT help: that file has exactly ONE "## " section ("## This session", 119035 of its 120183 bytes), so a drop-oldest-section pruner has nothing to drop and will hit the safe-fail path no matter which axis it measures. The two rows are complementary, not duplicates: this row fixes the actuator for every correctly-sectioned notebook, that row fixes the one file whose structure defeats any pruner. digest-predict (2 sections, one of which is a permanent "Known patterns / preferences" block) is marginal for the same reason and should be checked while working that row.

ADJACENT, DO NOT EXPAND SCOPE INTO IT: .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md AC-5 (:69-76) is also a line-only gate (`[ "$NB_LINES" -gt 200 ]`), so the composing agent's own pre-write check shares the blind spot. Fixing the actuator is sufficient to converge the files; aligning AC-5 is a cheap rider the implementer may take if it is one line, but it is not required for this row to close.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. A notebook at 150 lines and 40000 bytes is pruned until bytes <= 12000 (currently: untouched). Regression case for the byte axis.
  2. A notebook at 250 lines and 8000 bytes is still pruned to <= 200 lines (line axis not regressed).
  3. A notebook within BOTH caps is untouched — no false positive, mirroring test T4 in the existing context-bloat-backstop.test.sh suite.
  4. The single-section safe-fail path is covered by a test asserting the chosen option [a] or [b], and asserting NO mid-section truncation.
  5. Extend scripts/agents-flow/context-bloat-backstop.test.sh or add the sibling notebook-auto-prune test; a fix landing without a byte-axis test recreates the class the moment someone re-tunes the loop.
  6. Cited as instance 13 / sub-class 7 on SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP — do not close that reference when closing this row.
